issues.t: Speedometer and warning lights may not show at startup (recall)
issues.sym: When you start the car, the instrument display may not show your speed, the brake system warning light or the tire pressure warning light.
issues.why: A software error at startup can keep the instrument panel from displaying this information. Toyota recall 25V-595 covers the Crown along with many other Toyota and Lexus models.
issues.next: If the gauges are blank or missing after startup, don't drive until they come back. Check your VIN for open recalls; the fix is a free software update, done over the air or at a dealer.

issues.t: Backup camera may freeze or go blank (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the camera picture freezes or the screen stays blank.
issues.why: A software error in the parking assist system can freeze the rearview image. Recall 25V-744 covers cars with the panoramic view monitor across many 2022-2026 Toyota, Lexus and Subaru models.
issues.next: Until it is fixed, check mirrors and look over your shoulder when backing up, and don't rely on the screen. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer updates the software for free.

issues.t: Front or rear camera can short out from water inside (recall)
issues.sym: The rear or front camera image is blank, blurry or distorted.
issues.why: Weak laser welds on the camera housings can let water in and short the camera. Recall 24V-442 covers about 13,000 2023 Crowns.
issues.next: Use your mirrors and check around the car until it is fixed. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer inspects and replaces the cameras for free.

issues.t: Shudder or vibration at low speed (Hybrid MAX)
issues.sym: A vibration or shudder from the transmission when creeping in Drive or Reverse below about 8 mph, while the gas engine is running. The check engine light may come on with code P0840.
issues.why: Toyota issued service bulletins for this on some 2023 Crown Platinum (Hybrid MAX) cars. Some cars need a new transmission and transmission control module.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check it under warranty and ask about bulletins T-SB-0001-24 and T-TT-0740-23. Write down when it happens so the dealer can reproduce it.

issues.t: Hesitation or delay when pulling away from a stop
issues.sym: When you press the gas from a stop or at low speed, the car is slow to respond or pauses for a moment before it accelerates. This can feel unsafe when pulling into traffic.
issues.why: Owners of 2023-2025 Crowns have filed several complaints with NHTSA about this. Dealers often could not reproduce it, and Toyota has not published a cause.
issues.next: Leave extra room when pulling into traffic until it is checked. Report it to a Toyota dealer under warranty and note when it happens (cold engine, after braking, uphill). You can also file a complaint at nhtsa.gov.

issues.t: Low oil pressure warning and milky oil after short trips in the cold
issues.sym: An Oil Pressure Low message and check engine light (codes such as P0520 or P0524), and oil on the dipstick or under the filler cap that looks milky or tan.
issues.why: On short trips in very cold weather, moisture from the engine condenses in the oil instead of burning off. If it freezes, oil pressure can drop. Toyota issued a service bulletin for this on the 2.5L hybrid engine.
issues.next: If the oil pressure warning comes on, stop safely and turn off the engine. Have a Toyota dealer inspect it under warranty and ask about bulletin TSB010421. Longer drives now and then help clear moisture from the oil.

issues.t: Hybrid system warning light in freezing weather
issues.sym: The hybrid system warning comes on when it is below freezing, often at startup. Codes P1C84 or P3004 may be stored.
issues.why: Toyota issued a service bulletin for a false high-voltage circuit fault that can be set in temperatures below 32°F on some 2016-2023 hybrids.
issues.next: If the car won't go into Ready or drives poorly, don't keep driving; call for help. Otherwise have a Toyota dealer read the codes under warranty and ask about bulletin TSB008523A.

issues.t: Check engine light for a crankcase vent hose code (P2C90)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P2C90, saying a crankcase ventilation hose is disconnected, even though the hoses are fine.
issues.why: Toyota found the engine computer could set this code falsely and released updated software in a service bulletin.
issues.next: Have the hoses checked. If they are connected, ask a Toyota dealer for the software update in bulletin TSB010123 under warranty.

issues.t: Check engine light for a turbo wastegate code (P0243)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0243, for the turbocharger wastegate solenoid circuit.
issues.why: Toyota issued a service bulletin with updated engine computer software to reduce this code on 2023 Crowns. Only the Hybrid MAX engine has a turbo.
issues.next: Have the code read. If power feels normal it is not an emergency, but book a dealer visit for the software update in bulletin TSB009123.

issues.t: Heater blows cool after a hot restart
issues.sym: Right after restarting a warm car, the heater blows lukewarm or cool air until the gas engine kicks in.
issues.why: The hybrid system can stay in electric mode after a restart, so little engine heat reaches the heater. Toyota changed the engine computer logic in a service bulletin.
issues.next: If it bothers you or the windows fog, ask a Toyota dealer for the software update in bulletin T-SB-0014-24. Use the defroster setting to clear fogged glass.

issues.sym: Sudden warning lights, check engine light, or features that stop working, often after the car has been parked for a while. Chewed wires, nesting or droppings under the hood.
issues.why: Mice and rats can nest in the engine bay and chew through wires. Crown owners have reported this on very low-mileage cars, with major repairs, and warranty does not cover animal damage.
issues.next: Don't drive if warnings for brakes, steering or the hybrid system are on. Have a shop inspect the wiring, and ask your insurer, since comprehensive coverage often pays for animal damage. Rodent-deterrent tape or traps can help prevent repeat damage.

issues.t: Rocker or door molding coming loose
issues.sym: The trim strip along the bottom of the doors pulls away from the body, flaps or rattles at highway speed, or comes off.
issues.why: The molding is held on by clips that can let go. Owners report it on new cars, and a dealer said it had seen similar complaints.
issues.next: Push it back in place if it's only partly loose, and have a dealer re-secure it under warranty before it comes off on the road.

issues.sym: Apple CarPlay drops navigation or calls, the multimedia screen won't load your profile, or app and remote features don't work.
issues.why: Toyota issued bulletins for multimedia profile problems and connected-services faults on the 2023 Crown, and owners of later years report CarPlay dropouts.
issues.next: Restart the system and your phone, try another cable, and install any available software updates. If it continues, ask a dealer about the latest multimedia software.

issues.t: Load capacity label may show wrong numbers (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The label showing how much extra weight the car can carry may be wrong on cars with dealer-installed accessories.
issues.why: Gulf States Toyota recall 24V-548 covers cars with its accessories whose load labels show inaccurate weight values, which could lead to overloading.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; a correct label is mailed for free. Don't overload the car in the meantime.
